**Note**: You may use available tools or skills in the system to complete this task.

and you need to complete the task in 480s.

- Securities Market

- Market capitalisation was $45.9 trillion at the end of March 2026, an increase of 15 per cent from $40.0 trillion for the same period last year.

- The average daily turnover in March 2026 was $304.0 billion, an increase of 8 per cent from $280.2 billion for the same period last year.

- The average daily turnover for the first three months of 2026 was $276.7 billion, an increase of 14 per cent when compared with $242.7 billion for the same period last year.

- The average daily turnover of derivative warrants for the first three months of 2026 was $7.5 billion, an increase of 1 per cent when compared with $7.4 billion for the same period last year.

- The average daily turnover of CBBCs for the first three months of 2026 was $13.9 billion, an increase of 40 per cent when compared with $9.9 billion for the same period last year.

- The average daily turnover of ETFs for the first three months of 2026 was $40.2 billion, an increase of 15 per cent when compared with $35.0 billion for the same period last year.

- The average daily turnover of L&I Products for the first three months of 2026 was $4.9 billion, an increase of 11 per cent when compared with $4.4 billion for the same period last year.

- There were 40 newly listed companies for the first three months of 2026, an increase of 135 per cent when compared with 17* for the same period last year.

- Funds raised through IPOs# for the first three months of 2026 was $109.9 billion, an increase of 488 per cent when compared with $18.7 billion for the same period last year.

- Total funds raised for the first three months of 2026 was $150.2 billion.

- Derivatives Market

- The average daily volume of futures and options for the first three months of 2026 was 1,828,560 contracts.

- The average daily volume of Stock Options for the first three months of 2026 was 943,511 contracts.

China’s economy expanded 5% in the first quarter, accelerating from 4.5% in the prior quarter and beating expectations, as stronger exports helped offset still-muted domestic demand. Activity data for March painted a mixed picture, with industrial production holding up better than expected even as retail sales softened and unemployment edged higher. On the geopolitical front, Israel is weighing a possible ceasefire in Lebanon, while US President Donald Trump said the broader war with Iran could end soon as efforts to extend a fragile truce and restart negotiations continue. Notable gains were seen from Contemporary Amperex (5.5%), Zhongji Innolight (3.8%), Foxconn Industrial (2.6%), BYD (2.4%), and Zijin Mining (1.1%).
